description: Find movies like X, shows to watch after Y, or alternatives when someone liked one title but disliked another. Resolve names with search_titles first, then pass positive and disliked reference IDs plus any desired qualities. For open-ended or mood-only discovery without reference titles, use get_charts and choose from its viewing_experience context; this avoids relying on optional free-text encoding. Returns up to twelve candidates with ReelRecs Score, descriptions, genres, subgenres, subjects, tags, keywords, cast, directors, runtime, viewing_experience mood levels, reference overlaps and title links. General similarity supplies the neighborhood; intent selects the supporting evidence emphasis. Dislikes adjust comparable affinities; exclusions hide exact titles. Use mood_preferences for soft ordering by stored feelings, even when qualities_applied says the free-text ranking was unavailable. Provider filters apply in the requested country; country alone does not filter availability. No account required.

country.description: Two-letter availability country, such as US or GB. Use known location; US is the default. Does not establish availability unless providers are also supplied.
country.title: Country

exclude_ids.description: Resolved titles to leave out, including a viewer's 'seen it' reaction. Keep earlier constraints when refining. For disliked-title affinities, use avoid_seed_ids on recommend_titles or recommend_for_me instead.
exclude_ids.title: Exclude Ids

max_episode_minutes.description: Maximum runtime per episode in minutes. Does not describe a whole season or restrict films.
max_episode_minutes.title: Max Episode Minutes

max_movie_minutes.description: Maximum film runtime in minutes. Does not restrict series; set kind=movie for a movie-only request.
max_movie_minutes.title: Max Movie Minutes

providers.description: Streaming providers to require. Country and offer_types filter availability only when providers are supplied.
providers.title: Providers

year_from.description: Earliest original release year. A series uses its first-release year, not the year of a returning season or addition to a service.
year_from.title: Year From

avoid_seed_ids.description: Titles the viewer disliked. Reduces candidates closer to these than to the positive references. This differs from exclude_ids, which only hides exact titles. Uses exact versions; a title dislike alone does not specify an unwanted theme.
avoid_seed_ids.title: Avoid Seed Ids

intent.description: Evidence emphasis: watched for viewing, loved for ratings, into for topics and mood references. The general title neighborhood is shared. This field does not establish viewer history; qualities express the experience wanted.
intent.title: Intent

limit.description: Candidate shortlist size for the assistant to choose from, not the number to show the viewer. Usually retrieve twelve and present two or three fitting choices.
limit.title: Limit

mood_preferences.description: Optional soft viewing preferences inferred from what the viewer says, up to four feelings. For cozy and not sad, use calmness=high, warmth=high, sadness=low. Wonder means awe=high; a little tension means tension=moderate. Uses stored mood data without a text encoder. Preserve these through refinement. Do not ask the viewer for scores or infer a required genre. Unknown profiles remain eligible; this is not a content-safety filter or a guarantee.
mood_preferences.title: Mood Preferences

qualities.description: The experience wanted now: mood, tone, pace, themes and qualities to avoid, in natural language. Preserve refinements such as absorbing but not draining or more playful. This request does not change saved taste.
qualities.title: Qualities

seed_ids.description: Resolved positive reference titles. These can be viewer likes or assistant-chosen examples of a requested mood. A reference alone does not establish that the viewer watched or liked it.
seed_ids.title: Seed Ids

name: recommend_titles
title: Find what to watch next
